text_blocks.snippet: A PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) test is a laboratory technique used to detect and amplify specific pieces of genetic material, such as DNA or RNA, from a sample. In the context of infections, PCR is used to identify the presence of pathogens like viruses or bacteria by detecting their unique genetic material. This makes PCR a valuable tool for diagnosing various infections early, even before the body develops a strong immune response.
snippet_highlighted_words: used to identify the presence of pathogens like viruses or bacteria by detecting their unique genetic material

list.title: Amplification:
list.snippet: PCR works by creating multiple copies of a specific DNA or RNA sequence, making it easier to detect even if the initial amount of genetic material is very small.

list.title: Infectious Disease Diagnosis:
list.snippet: PCR is widely used to diagnose infectious diseases, including COVID-19, influenza, and other viral and bacterial infections.

list.title: Early Detection:
list.snippet: Because PCR amplifies the genetic material, it can detect infections earlier than other methods like antibody tests, which rely on the body's immune response.

list.title: Pathogen Identification:
list.snippet: PCR can identify specific pathogens by targeting unique sequences in their DNA or RNA, helping to differentiate between similar organisms.

list.title: Other Applications:
list.snippet: PCR is also used in other areas, such as cancer diagnosis and genetic testing, but its use in detecting infections is particularly prominent.
